name: Burgess Falls State Park
customer: Hikers, photographers, families with older children
unique: Four waterfalls stacked in a row on Falling Water River, ending in a hundred and thirty foot drop into a gorge, with a staircase and overlooks that put you above the lip of the last one.
buzz: The overlooks are the easy version and the base trail is the hard one, and people are explicit that the stairs are steep. Spring runoff is the season.

name: Cookeville Depot Museum
unique: A 1909 Tennessee Central depot with the original ticket window and telegraph office, a model railroad, and a red caboose on the track outside that children are allowed to climb through.
buzz: The caboose is the reason families stop and the depot is the reason they stay. Volunteers run it and will tell you which train came through when.

name: Window Cliffs State Natural Area
company: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation
unique: A five and a half mile hike with eighteen creek crossings to a ridge of rock with natural windows punched through it, above the confluence of Cane Creek and the Caney Fork.
buzz: The crossings are the story, and people say to wear shoes you do not mind soaking. The cliffs at the end are unlike anything else in the region.

name: Cookeville Downtown and WestSide
unique: A courthouse square with a depot district a few blocks west, in a town that grew where the railroad crossed the Walton Road, with a restored theater, a local food scene and a depot that still has tracks behind it.
buzz: Cookeville is the biggest town on the Cumberland Plateau and the square shows it. People stop on the way to the falls and end up eating downtown.

name: Cummins Falls State Park
cost: Free, gorge access permit required in season
dates: Year round; base access by permit March to October
unique: A seventy five foot waterfall on the Blackburn Fork, with a plunge pool you can swim in at the bottom of a gorge reached by a steep, wet, rope assisted descent that the state now limits with permits to keep the rescues down.
buzz: People who go say the swim under the falls is worth the climb back up and that the permit system made it bearable. The overlook trail is the dry alternative and still gives the view.

name: Gainesboro Courthouse Square
unique: A square on a bluff over the Cumberland with a 1920s courthouse, mom and pop stores and a restaurant or two, in the county seat that floods when the river comes up.
buzz: Small and genuinely lived in. People stop on the way to Cummins Falls and find the square emptier and friendlier than they expected.

name: Historic Granville
dates: Museum Wednesday to Saturday; village year round
unique: A river village that has preserved its 1880s storefronts, a general store still selling hardware and bologna, a homestead with outbuildings and a museum of quilts and farm life, and calls itself Tennessee's Mayberry.
buzz: The Sutton Store is the anchor and the volunteers are the reason it works. People come for Heritage Day in May and come back for the quiet.

name: Poke Sallet Festival
unique: Tennessee's original poke sallet festival, built around a wild green that has to be boiled three times to be safe, with a cooking contest, music on the square and a parade through Gainesboro.
buzz: The dish is the joke and the tradition at once, and locals defend it. The festival is the county's homecoming and the square is full by noon.

name: Edgar Evins State Park
unique: Sixty three hundred acres on Center Hill Lake where the cabins and cabanas are built on stilts down a steep hillside to the water, so you park at the top and walk down to a deck over the lake.
buzz: The hillside cabanas are the reason people book a year out, and the observation tower at the visitor center is the free version of the same view. The marina rents pontoons.

name: Appalachian Center for Craft
dur: 1-2 hours or a multi day class
dates: Gallery weekdays, workshops spring to fall
customer: Craft students, artists, couples looking for a weekend class
unique: A craft school on a bluff over Center Hill Lake with studios for blacksmithing, glass, clay, wood and fibers, a gallery of student and resident work and summer workshops where anybody can spend a week learning to blow glass or forge a blade.
buzz: Students come from other states for the workshops and the setting is half of it. Visitors who only stop at the gallery are surprised by how much is made on site.

name: Smithville Courthouse Square
unique: A square with an 1870s courthouse, a ring of shops and a mural or two, in the town that hosts the fiddler's jamboree and sits between the lake and the plateau.
buzz: The square is small and the people are used to lake traffic. It is a good place to buy a sandwich before the craft center.

name: Center Hill Lake
dates: Year round, best May to October
unique: A deep, clear Corps lake on the Caney Fork with more than four hundred miles of wooded shoreline, houseboat rentals, and coves where the water is green enough to see twenty feet down.
buzz: Boaters call it the prettiest lake in middle Tennessee and the houseboat weekends book early. Anglers fish the ledges for bass and walleye.

name: Virgin Falls State Natural Area
company: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation
unique: A river that rises from a cave, drops a hundred and ten feet over a cliff and disappears into another cave at the bottom, reached by a nine mile round trip with two other waterfalls along the way.
buzz: Hikers describe it as the best hard day hike in the state and warn about the climb out. Overnight camping is allowed and the falls run strongest in winter and spring.

name: Sparta Liberty Square
unique: A courthouse square with a ring of shops and galleries, in a town laid out in 1806 that still holds a Liberty Square Christmas and a summer concert series on the lawn.
buzz: Quieter than Cookeville and better for browsing. People pair it with a hike and say the square is the surprise of the county.

name: White County Heritage Museum
unique: A county museum a block off the square, holding the photographs, tools, uniforms and household goods of a county that has been farming, milling and digging caves for two centuries.
buzz: Volunteers open it and walk you through. Small towns like this have one room of everything and the person who knows what it all is.

name: Cumberland Caverns
unique: More than thirty miles of surveyed passage under Cardwell Mountain, with a walking tour through the Volcano Room where the floor is a hundred feet wide and concerts were staged for years before the bigger cave venue opened down the road.
buzz: The walking tour is the family version and the wild tour is the one people brag about. Guides turn off the lights at one point and the darkness is the memory.

name: Rock Island State Park
dates: Year round; water releases affect access
unique: Where the Collins and Caney Fork meet in a gorge below Great Falls Dam, with Twin Falls pouring out of the rock across the river, a blue green swimming hole and a nineteenth century cotton mill village site above the water.
buzz: Swimmers love the blue hole and photographers come for Twin Falls when the dam is releasing. Kayakers run the gorge below when the water is right, and the steps down are steep.

name: McMinnville Courthouse Square
unique: A square in the self declared nursery capital of the world, with a 1930s courthouse and storefronts, and garden centers and nurseries ringing the town in every direction.
buzz: The nurseries are the real attraction and the square is the stop before them. People drive in for plants and leave with a truckload.

name: Defeated Creek Park
company: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Cordell Hull Lake
unique: A Corps campground on the Cordell Hull Lake shoreline with sites that back up to the water, a swimming beach, a boat ramp and the kind of shade and quiet that fills reservations six months ahead.
buzz: Regulars book the same site every year and say the lake level makes or breaks the view. It is the summer camping default for half of Smith County.

name: Carthage Courthouse Square
unique: A square above the Cumberland with an 1800s courthouse, a Civil War hospital story in the buildings around it, and the law office town where Cordell Hull practiced before he became secretary of state.
buzz: Quiet and intact and easy to walk in half an hour. The river view at the end of the street is the reward.

name: Cordell Hull Lake
dates: Year round, best spring to fall
unique: A Corps lake on the Cumberland with more than three hundred miles of shoreline, flooded timber at the upper end that holds crappie and bass, and a dam and lock that keep the river working.
buzz: Crappie anglers fish the brush in spring and the lake is big enough to disappear on. Birders work the upper coves where the herons nest.

name: Red Boiling Springs
unique: A mineral springs resort town that once drew thousands a summer by train, where three of the old hotels still take guests, the spring water still runs out of a pipe downtown and the pace has not changed since the 1930s.
buzz: People come for the porches and the rocking chairs and stay for dinner at a communal table. It is the last of Tennessee's mineral springs resorts and the town is proud without being precious about it.

name: The Armour Hotel
unique: One of the three surviving resort hotels in Red Boiling Springs, with a long porch, a lobby full of old furniture and photographs, home cooked meals served at set times and a mineral bath down the street.
buzz: Guests describe it as staying at a grandmother's house at scale, with breakfast included and nothing to do but sit. Rooms are plain and that is the point.

name: Lafayette Courthouse Square
unique: A square with a 1900s courthouse and a ring of stores in a county that grows tobacco, corn and cattle and sends its children to a high school in the same town.
buzz: Small, tidy and unhurried. People stop on the way to Red Boiling Springs and find the courthouse lawn shaded and empty.

name: Dale Hollow Lake
cost: Free, marina and camping fees extra
dates: Year round, best May to October
unique: Twenty seven thousand acres of deep, clear water on the Obey River where the world record smallmouth bass was caught in 1955, with houseboat rentals, cliff lined coves and more than six hundred miles of shoreline.
buzz: Smallmouth anglers treat it as a pilgrimage and boaters rent houseboats for a week at a time. The water is clear enough that people swim off the back of the boat in the middle of the lake.

name: Clay County Museum of History
unique: A downtown museum of a county that was cut off by ridges until the lake and the highway came, with farm tools, photographs, quilts and the records of the river landings that are now under water.
buzz: Volunteers run it and know the family names. It is small, free and the best way to understand why the lake changed everything here.

name: Chocolate Gravy Festival
unique: A one day festival devoted to chocolate gravy, the Cumberland Plateau breakfast of cocoa, sugar and butter poured over a hot biscuit, with a cooking contest, vendors and a lot of biscuits.
buzz: People who grew up with it come home for it and people who did not come to find out what it is. The contest table is the first place to go.

name: Celina Courthouse Square
unique: A square a few blocks from the Dale Hollow dam and the Cumberland River, with a 1930s courthouse, a monument and the storefronts of a town that rebuilt after the lake took the bottomland.
buzz: It is five minutes from the water and most boaters never see it. The square is quiet and the courthouse lawn looks over the roofs toward the river.
